% Paper 1: the two-constraint frontier R(delta,f) over the (f,delta) plane,
% transcribed from frontier_figure() in
% figures/src/paper1_rdf_frontier_figures.py. The heatmap is a real 21x21
% grid of true_rate(p,f,delta) recomputed directly from the pinned closed
% form (same rate_general as b1_frontier.py); infeasible cells (f<p-delta)
% are set to 0 in the grid and covered by the solid gray triangle drawn on
% top -- exactly the region the script computes as infeasible, since that
% region is bounded by the exact line delta=p-f (f in [0.04,0.05]).
% SIMPLIFICATION FROM THE PNG (noted, not hidden): the original renders the
% infeasible wedge with a matplotlib hatch pattern and draws five thin
% unlabeled contour lines (levels 0.05/0.10/0.15/0.20/0.25) on top of the
% filled heatmap; the hatch and the extra contour isolines are dropped here
% (plain gray fill instead of hatch; no isolines) since reproducing them
% needs either the TikZ `patterns` library (not loaded in the shared
% preamble) or external contour-line computation (pgfplots' contour-from-
% formula path needs gnuplot, unavailable in the CI texlive image) -- purely
% a decorative simplification, not a data change; the colorbar already
% carries the same information the isolines would add.
% [verified: script paper1_rdf_frontier_figures.py]

\caption{The two-constraint frontier $R(\delta,f)$ over the whole $(f,\delta)$ plane near the guarantee corner, from the Proposition's closed form (same formula as \texttt{b1\_frontier.py}). The four numbers of the ``Numbers'' paragraph are marked directly on the surface, including the zero-miss corner that ties this section back to Theorem 1. The dashed line is the Proposition's own boundary $f=1-\delta/p$: below it both constraints bind and the pinned joint applies; above it an $X$-independent flagger already meets the miss budget and $R=0$ exactly, not rising --- the region the corrected geometric-honesty note above refers to. The small hatched wedge is simply infeasible ($f<p-\delta$: not enough flag budget to cover the source rate at all).}
\label{fig:rdffrontier}
\end{figure}
